program_name: Archival Science and AI (Italian page title: "Archival science and AI"; full descriptive title used by the University: "Archival science and artificial intelligence"). Laurea Magistrale / Second Cycle Degree, 2 years, 120 ECTS. First programme in Italy combining archival science with artificial intelligence.
teaching_language: fully English - the programme is delivered entirely in English ("un corso internazionale, erogato interamente in lingua inglese presso la sede di Rieti"). Note the delivery MODE is blended/'mixed' (modalita 'mista'): for activities other than practical and laboratory work, up to two-thirds of the teaching may be delivered by distance/telematic means. This is a delivery-mode caveat, not a language caveat. Coursework, the admission interview and the didactic regulation all reference English as the language of instruction; only administrative/regulatory documents (Regolamento didattico) are published in Italian.
campus: Rieti - Polo Universitario di Rieti (Rieti Campus), Dipartimento di Scienze giuridiche, sociali e pedagogiche (DIKE - Department of Legal, Social and Educational Sciences). Departmental administrative seat: Via Santa Maria in Gradi 4 / Largo dell'Universita, 01100 Viterbo. Student Office tel. 0761 357604 / 0761 357898 / 0761 357494; didactics email didattica.dike@unitus.it; administrative secretariat amministrazione.dike@unitus.it.
degree_class: LM-5 (Archivistica e biblioteconomia / Archival and Library Science)
academic_requirements:
AD ACCESSO LIBERO (open access) - Art. 5 of the didactic regulation states: "Il Corso di Laurea Magistrale e ad accesso libero." There is no numero programmato, no ranking and no TOLC. Curricular requirements are verified at enrolment by a Teaching Commission (Commissione didattica). Requirements (identical in the Italian and English versions of the official Admission Requirements document, and in the D.R. 193/2026 didactic regulation):
1) FIRST-LEVEL DEGREE: possession of a first-cycle/bachelor's degree of at least 180 CFU/ECTS obtained at an Italian university, or an equivalent foreign qualification recognised as suitable ("riconosciuto come idoneo"). Foreign qualifications follow the standard UNITUS route: Declaration of Value from the Italian consulate, or a CIMEA Statement of Comparability, or an ARDI Statement of Correspondence, or a legalised Diploma Supplement.
2) MINIMUM 90 CFU/ECTS IN LISTED SSD (scientific-disciplinary sectors). The list is broad and humanities/law/social-science weighted, with two computing sectors: INF/01 (Computer Science) and ING-INF/05 (Information Processing Systems); IUS/01, IUS/08, IUS/09, IUS/10, IUS/14, IUS/18, IUS/19, IUS/20, IUS/21 (law); L-ANT/01 to L-ANT/10 (antiquities/archaeology); L-ART/01 to L-ART/08 (art, music, cinema); L-FIL-LET/01 to L-FIL-LET/15 (philology and literature); L-LIN/01 to L-LIN/21 (linguistics and modern languages); L-OR/01, L-OR/10, L-OR/23 (oriental studies); M-FIL/05 to M-FIL/08 (philosophy); M-DEA/01 (anthropology); M-GGR/01, M-GGR/02 (geography); M-STO/01 to M-STO/09 (history, including M-STO/08 archival science, bibliography and library science and M-STO/09 palaeography); SECS-P/04, SECS-P/08, SECS-P/12 (economics/management); SPS/01 to SPS/14 (political and social sciences).
3) TOLERANCE: "A tolerance of up to a maximum of 10% of the required ECTS credits is allowed" - i.e. roughly 81 CFU can be accepted instead of 90 at the Commission's discretion.
4) PERSONAL PREPARATION: the Commissione didattica verifies the curricular requirements and the candidate's personal preparation on the basis of the curriculum vitae et studiorum, supplemented by an interview (see entry_exam_or_test). The Commission also sets the procedures for recovering any missing credits, in accordance with the course's Academic Regulations.
No minimum GPA / final-mark threshold is published anywhere in the official documents. The exact SSD list is anchored to the SUA-CdS of the academic year of enrolment, so it can change year to year.
language_requirements: English at CEFR B2 minimum, evidenced in one of two ways, per the official Admission Requirements document: "Proficiency in English at least at the B2 level (Common European Framework of Reference for Languages), certified by an appropriate language certification or, in the absence of such certification, by passing a specific test organized by the Department." This is a PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC ADDITION to the university baseline: DIKE runs its own in-house English test for candidates who hold no certificate, so a certificate is not strictly mandatory. University-wide accepted certificates (baseline, unchanged for this programme): IELTS, TOEFL, TCL, Cambridge First, PTE Academic, Oxford Test of English, Aptis ESOL General/Advanced; an EMI (English as Medium of Instruction) certificate attesting that previous university study was delivered in English is also accepted in place of a test certificate. No specific minimum band/score table is published for this programme - only the B2 CEFR level. No Italian language requirement: the programme is delivered entirely in English and no Italian test is required for English-taught programmes at UNITUS.
entry_exam_or_test:
No competitive entrance exam, no TOLC, no ranking - admission is open. Instead there is an ORAL ADMISSION INTERVIEW conducted in English:
- The official Admission Requirements document states: "A Teaching Commission will be established to verify the admission requirements and, during an interview (conducted in English and possibly remotely), assess the candidate's personal preparation." The Italian text specifies "in sede di colloquio (svolto in lingua inglese anche a distanza)" - i.e. it may be held remotely/online.
- FORMAT: oral, in English, may be held at a distance (video call). The Commission assesses personal preparation, not a syllabus-based exam; no published pass mark, no published topic list, no published interview dates or sessions.
- BOOKING: the programme page links a Google Form under "Admission: Oral interview". Current a.y. 2026/2027 form (international students only): https://forms.gle/CiZaCwvFvptHbcDc9 - AS ACCESSED ON 2026-09-05 THIS FORM IS CLOSED, titled "Archival Science and AI 2026/2027 a.y. - Admissions closed for the 2026/2027 a.y. for extra EU students". A second, older interview-booking form (a.y. 2025/2026) at https://forms.gle/5r6bbPkWYT4WgseR8 is also closed ("Admissions closed for extra-EU students - Archival science and AI 2025/2026 a.y. - Admission Interview Booking").
- OFA / MISSING CREDITS: if curricular credits are missing, the Commissione didattica sets the recovery procedures under the course regulation (Art. 5, D.R. 193/2026 of 13/04/2026). No fixed OFA scheme is published.
- NOTE ON WORDING: the didactic regulation phrases the interview as conditional - "la sua personale preparazione sulla base del curriculum vitae et studiorum, eventualmente integrato da un colloquio" (personal preparation assessed on the CV, possibly supplemented by an interview) - while the Admission Requirements document and the course page present the oral interview as the operative admission step. In practice international applicants must book the interview via the Google Form. [uncertain]
application_deadline_eu: Academic year 2026/2027. No programme-specific application deadline for EU/Italy-resident candidates - the programme is open access and follows the university-wide calendar (rolling). Enrolment 2026-08-01 to 2026-12-29 (deadline for 1st-year Master's students); 2026-11-04 is the deadline for bachelor's and for 2nd-year-and-beyond master's students (plus first instalment); extension to 2027-02-28 for candidates graduating in January/February 2027. Curricular requirements and personal preparation are verified by the Commissione didattica at the time of enrolment, so an interview should be booked before the enrolment deadline. No separate EU-only form or session is published on the programme page. [uncertain]

required_documents: Programme-specific: completed Admission Form / oral-interview booking form for international students, linked from the course page (a.y. 2026/2027 form: https://forms.gle/CiZaCwvFvptHbcDc9 - closed for extra-EU students as of 2026-09-05).
Bachelor's degree (first-level degree) of at least 180 CFU/ECTS - certified copy with Apostille/legalisation and certified Italian translation, OR a CIMEA Statement of Verification.

Transcript of Records - required to evidence the minimum 90 CFU in the listed SSD sectors (10% tolerance applies); the Commissione didattica maps foreign coursework onto the Italian SSD list, so a detailed, subject-by-subject transcript with credit values is effectively essential for this programme.

Curriculum vitae et studiorum - explicitly named in Art. 5 of the didactic regulation as the basis on which the Commissione didattica assesses personal preparation. This is a programme-specific addition to the university baseline.
Declaration of Value from the Italian consulate, OR CIMEA Statement of Comparability, OR ARDI Statement of Correspondence.
Diploma Supplement (can replace the Declaration of Value if legalised).
High school diploma (certified copy + Apostille/legalisation + certified Italian translation, or CIMEA Statement of Verification).

English language certification at CEFR B2 or above, OR an EMI (English as Medium of Instruction) certificate from previous university study. If the candidate holds neither, the Department organises its own English test in place of a certificate - programme-specific.
Admission letter (issued after the interview / verification of requirements).
Passport / identity document, and for non-EU applicants the Universitaly pre-enrolment printout and study visa; proof of financial means of EUR 10,179.85 per year for the visa application.
tuition_or_fees_link: https://www.unitus.it/en/students/fees-and-contributions/ - UNITUS uses an ISEEUP income-based model for EU/resident students (regional tax and stamp duty always due; contribution scaled by ISEE bracket, with full exemption 'no tax area' at the lowest brackets). Non-EU students who cannot produce an ISEE are charged a flat band by country of origin: EUR 600 / 1,050 / 1,500 / 1,950 per year. Full rules: https://www.unitus.it/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/TUITION-FEES-AND-CONTRIBUTIONS-REGULATIONS_2026-2027.pdf ; simulator: https://www.unitus.it/en/students/fees-and-contributions/tuition-fee-simulator/ . No programme-specific fee or surcharge is published for Archival Science and AI.

uncertainty_notes:
1) NON-EU ADMISSIONS ARE CLOSED FOR 2026/2027. This is the single most important caveat for ItalyPath users. The programme's own admission form (the only route published on the course page) is titled "Admissions closed for the 2026/2027 a.y. for extra EU students" as of 2026-09-05. UNITUS publishes NO closing date, no reopening date, and no explanation anywhere on unitus.it - only the closed form state. The identical pattern is visible on the previous cycle's 2025/2026 form, so an early, unpublished non-EU cut-off appears to be this programme's standing practice. Do not present the university-wide 2026-12-29 / 2026-11-30 dates to non-EU users for this programme without this warning.
2) NO PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC DEADLINE DATES ARE PUBLISHED AT ALL, for EU or non-EU. Both deadline fields are therefore built from the verified university-wide 2026/2027 calendar plus the observed closed state of the programme form. Both are marked uncertain.
3) OFFICIAL CALL: no bando / call for applications exists - the programme is ad accesso libero, consistent with all other UNITUS LM programmes. official_call_url therefore holds the Italian didactic regulation PDF (Regolamento didattico, D.R. n. 193/2026 of 13/04/2026), which is the authoritative admission document, not a call.
4) MILD CONTRADICTION ON THE INTERVIEW. The didactic regulation (Art. 5.3) describes the interview as conditional - personal preparation assessed on the CV, "eventualmente integrato da un colloquio" (possibly supplemented by an interview). The official Admission Requirements document and the course page instead present the oral interview as the operative step ("Admission: Oral interview", with a dedicated booking form). Treat the interview as required in practice for international applicants, but note the regulation leaves the Commission discretion.
5) NO ENGLISH-LANGUAGE SCORE TABLE. Only "CEFR B2" is stated; no IELTS/TOEFL minimum bands are published for this programme. The programme-specific alternative - a departmental English test in place of a certificate - is an addition to the shared UNITUS baseline and is confirmed in both the Italian and English versions of the Admission Requirements document.
6) SSD LIST IS YEAR-DEPENDENT. The regulation anchors the 90-CFU sector list to the SUA-CdS of the year of enrolment; the enumerated list transcribed here comes from the Admission Requirements PDF dated December 2025 (used for 2026/2027). It could be revised for later years.
7) NO GPA / MINIMUM MARK THRESHOLD is published in any official source; none was invented.
8) NO CURRICULA OR TRACKS are published - the programme appears to be single-track. No curricula list was found on the course page, the brochure or the regulation.
9) BLENDED DELIVERY. Up to two-thirds of non-practical teaching may be delivered remotely (modalita 'mista'). Students expecting a fully on-campus experience in Rieti should be told this. It is a delivery-mode caveat only - the language is fully English.
10) The English course page links the Admission Requirements as a .docx dated 2025/03 (https://www.unitus.it/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Requisiti-di-accesso-Admission-Requirements-Lm-5.docx) while the indexed and more recent version is the 2025/12 PDF used here; content of the PDF is bilingual (Italian + English) and was read in full.
11) The DIKE regulations page is server-rendered and the regulation PDF was read directly; no JS-blocked content affected this research.
